title: Slope-decay latency runs - quick lab log
content:
Goal: test how gradual decaying QPS ramps (slope decay) interact with cold/warm KV cache and autoscaling thresholds. Want to find knee where p95 jumps and where autoscaler fires spurious scale-ups during tail bursts.

Environment
- Model: open-llama-13b (int8/ptq) + kv-cache enabled
- Hardware: A100-40GB (shared pool), 4 replicas behind router
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.17.2, batching=continuous, batch_timeout_ms=8
- Test driver: locust-based harness (script attached in GH PR)

Protocol
1) Start with cold instances (no KV priming)
2) Ramp QPS linearly from 50 -> 1800 over 30 minutes (slope-decay)
3) Hold at peak for 5 min, then decay linear back to 50 over 10 min
4) Repeat with pre-warmed KV cache and with quantized vs fp16 variant

Quick results (aggregated windows, approximate)
- cold-run (no cache): p50=85ms, p95=420ms, p99=860ms at peak ~1800 qps
- warm-kv: p50=68ms, p95=210ms, p99=340ms at same peak
- fp16 variant: p95 improved ~12% vs int8 at mid-range QPS, but int8 wins at peak due to higher throughput
- autoscaler: fired an extra scale event on decay phase ~2x (oscillation) when cooldown=30s; increasing cooldown to 120s removed oscillation but raised p95 slightly during sudden second surge

Observations / hypotheses
- Slope (gradual ramp) exposes a narrow band (350-700 qps) where batch assembly increases latency variability because batch formation crosses small-request threshold -> p95 spikes. This is reproducible across runs.
- KV priming reduces p99 dramatically; likely because cache-miss penalty interacts with batch timeout causing long tail.
- Autoscaler config is too sensitive to the momentary sustained QPS during slope-back phase; need hysteresis or request-rate smoothing at router level rather than raw QPS threshold.

Quick ascii summary (p95 at sample QPS points):
QPS: 200 -> 600 -> 1200 -> 1800
p95: 110ms -> 260ms -> 370ms -> 420ms (cold)
       90ms  -> 160ms -> 220ms -> 210ms (warm)

Immediate next steps
- Run controlled micro-run where batch_timeout_ms = [4,8,16] to verify batch timeout tradeoffs in the 350-700 band (priority).
- Try router-level exponential smoothing over 30s / 60s windows and re-run slope-decay to observe autoscaler behavior.
- Add a run with KV pre-warm but with small synthetic cache churn to mimic tenant noise.

Questions to answer in followups
- What is the nominal customer experience boundary (p95 SLA) we want to keep under 250ms for this model family? If yes, we need a config recommendation.
- Would applying small-request batching opt-out for requests < token threshold help reduce variance? Costly but might improve p95.

Notes to self
- attach raw CSVs from locust as linked artifact in the PR (done)
- sync findings with Noah (obs) and SRE about cooldown/hysteresis before changing prod configs

Unresolved: edge-case where p99 stays >700ms intermittently even with warm-kv; collect heap/proc metrics in next run to see GC / GPU memory spikes.

End of quick log.
